subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
past_paper_reference: CUET UG Political Science Past Papers (2022-2024)

questions.question: Which historic constitutional provision was invoked for the first time in July 1959 to dismiss the democratically elected CPI government led by E.M.S. Namboodiripad in Kerala?
options: A) Article 356 (President's Rule)
B) Article 352 (National Emergency)
C) Article 360 (Financial Emergency)
D) Article 370 (Special Status)
questions.explanation: In July 1959, the central government dismissed the first communist ministry in Kerala under Article 356 following the Congress-led 'Vimochana Samaram' (Liberation Struggle).

questions.question: On which exact date did Maharaja Hari Singh of Jammu and Kashmir sign the Instrument of Accession to the Dominion of India following the Pakistani tribal invasion?
options: A) 15 August 1947
B) 26 October 1947
C) 26 January 1950
D) 1 January 1948
questions.explanation: Facing an imminent invasion by Pakistani-backed armed tribal raiders, Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession on 26 October 1947, requesting Indian military defense.

questions.question: In which district of Rajasthan was the modern three-tier Panchayati Raj system first inaugurated in India by Jawaharlal Nehru on 2 October 1959?
options: A) Jaipur
B) Ajmer
C) Nagaur
D) Bikaner
questions.explanation: Following recommendations of the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee, Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru inaugurated democratic decentralization (Panchayati Raj) at Nagaur, Rajasthan, on 2 October 1959.

questions.question: What was the official code name of the Indian Army's mission that evicted Pakistani regular troops and intruders from the heights of Kargil in July 1999?
options: A) Operation Meghdoot
B) Operation Cactus
C) Operation Parakram
D) Operation Vijay
questions.explanation: The Indian military offensive to recapture the high-altitude posts in the Kargil, Drass, and Batalik sectors occupied by Pakistani forces in 1999 was code-named Operation Vijay.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Which young socialist parliamentarians within the Congress, including Chandra Shekhar and Mohan Dharia, pressed Indira Gandhi for radical land reforms and bank nationalisation?
options: A) The 'Young Turks'
B) The Syndicate
C) The Swatantra Lobby
D) The Old Guard
questions.explanation: The 'Young Turks' was the popular moniker given to progressive socialist leaders within the Congress like Chandra Shekhar, Mohan Dharia, and Krishna Kant who pushed for radical socialist policies.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Chief Justice of India in April 1973, superseding three senior-most judges of the Supreme Court following the Kesavananda Bharati verdict?
options: A) Justice M.H. Beg
B) Justice A.N. Ray
C) Justice H.R. Khanna
D) Justice P.N. Bhagwati
questions.explanation: Breaking with the long-established convention of seniority, the government appointed Justice A.N. Ray as Chief Justice of India on 25 April 1973, superseding Justices Shelat, Hegde, and Grover.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: On which date did East Germany officially dissolve and reunite with West Germany, ending four decades of Cold War division?
options: A) 9 November 1989
B) 25 December 1991
C) 3 October 1990
D) 1 January 1993
questions.explanation: German reunification officially took effect on 3 October 1990, less than a year after the fall of the Berlin Wall, when East Germany acceded to the Federal Republic of Germany.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: Which distinguished Swedish diplomat served as the second Secretary-General of the United Nations, dying in an airplane crash in Africa in September 1961?
options: A) Trygve Lie
B) U Thant
C) Kurt Waldheim
D) Dag Hammarskjold
questions.explanation: Dag Hammarskjold served as UN Secretary-General from 1953 until he died in a tragic plane crash while on a peace mission to the Congo in September 1961, and was posthumously awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.

questions.question: During the preparation of the first national electoral roll for the 1951-1952 general elections, what major social issue did Chief Election Commissioner Sukumar Sen confront regarding female voters?
options: A) Nearly 2.8 million women were registered merely as 'wife of X' or 'daughter of Y' rather than by their own individual names, and Sen refused to accept these entries
B) Women across rural India organized violent boycotts demanding separate female polling booths in every village
C) The Constitution of India initially barred married women from voting unless their husbands consented in writing
D) Only women who owned registered landed property were permitted to cast their ballots in 1952
questions.explanation: Sukumar Sen insisted on individual dignity, refusing to accept rolls where 2.8 million women were listed only by relational identities, ordering them struck off unless individually identified.

questions.question: How did the States Reorganisation Commission (SRC) of 1953 handle the contentious demand of 'one language, one state' across India?
options: A) It recommended the immediate partitioning of India into over 100 independent sovereign linguistic kingdoms
B) It rejected the strict 'one language, one state' formula, recommending that language should be a primary consideration but balanced with administrative efficiency and national unity
C) It completely banned the use of any regional language in state administrations across India
D) It ordered that all state boundaries must remain strictly frozen according to British colonial provinces
questions.explanation: The SRC recognized the linguistic principle as a rational basis for reorganising states, but explicitly rejected the extreme concept of 'one language, one state' to prevent parochial balkanization.

questions.question: Why did the Government of India's radical policy of nationalising the wholesale trade in wheat in April 1973 fail, forcing its withdrawal the following year?
options: A) The United Nations imposed a total international embargo on Indian agricultural shipments
B) The Supreme Court of India declared all public food corporations unconstitutional under Article 19
C) Private grain traders and rich farmers hoarded wheat, state procurement fell dramatically short, and black-market grain prices skyrocketed
D) A sudden surplus of grain collapsed food prices and caused nationwide bankruptcy of state cooperatives
questions.explanation: Indira Gandhi's takeover of wholesale wheat trade in 1973 failed due to fierce trader resistance, hoarding by prosperous peasants, and inadequate state storage infrastructure, forcing its abandonment in 1974.

questions.question: What was the 'Forward Policy' adopted by the Indian military along the disputed northern borders with China between 1960 and 1962?
options: A) Launching preemptive air strikes against Chinese airbases in Lhasa and Chengdu
B) Signing a mutual defense treaty with Taiwan to initiate joint amphibious landings
C) Withdrawing all Indian border garrisons 100 miles south into the Brahmaputra plains
D) Establishing military outposts and patrols forward in disputed territories to establish physical presence, often flanking Chinese positions
questions.explanation: Under the Forward Policy, Indian forces established small forward patrol posts in the disputed border areas to prevent further Chinese territorial creeping, despite lacking adequate logistic backing.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: In the fifth General Election of 1971, how did the electoral performance of Indira Gandhi's Congress(R) fundamentally transform the party system?
options: A) It shattered the Grand Alliance, secured 352 Lok Sabha seats on its own, and restored Congress hegemony under a highly personalized, centralized leadership
B) It forced Congress to permanently enter into a national coalition government with the Swatantra Party
C) It resulted in a hung Parliament where the Communist Party of India held the balance of power
D) It led to the immediate dissolution of all state assemblies across southern India
questions.explanation: The 1971 victory restored the dominance of the Congress, but in a fundamentally transformed shape: highly centralized around Indira Gandhi's personal charisma, eclipsing internal party democracy.

questions.question: What was the core principle laid down by the Supreme Court in the historic Kesavananda Bharati judgment of 24 April 1973?
options: A) Parliament possesses absolute, unlimited power to repeal the entire Constitution and declare a monarchy
B) Parliament has the power to amend any part of the Constitution, but cannot alter its 'Basic Structure'
C) Fundamental Rights can never be amended or altered under any circumstances whatsoever
D) The Prime Minister of India possesses the supreme constitutional authority to override judicial rulings
questions.explanation: In Kesavananda Bharati (1973), a 13-judge bench established by a 7-6 majority that while Article 368 gives Parliament wide amending powers, it cannot alter or abrogate the 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution.

questions.question: What major electoral consequence followed the 1974 Navnirman movement in Gujarat led by students and supported by Morarji Desai's fast unto death?
options: A) Gujarat was partitioned into three separate Union Territories administered directly from New Delhi
B) The Supreme Court dismissed the Governor and appointed a judicial committee to govern the state
C) The state assembly was dissolved, fresh elections were held in June 1975, and the Congress was defeated by the opposition Janata Morcha coalition
D) Indira Gandhi immediately stepped down as Prime Minister and retired from politics
questions.explanation: Morarji Desai went on an indefinite hunger strike demanding early assembly elections; in the June 1975 elections, the opposition Janata Morcha defeated the Congress in Gujarat.

questions.question: In the context of the Punjab crisis, what was the 'Dharam Yudh Morcha' launched by the Shiromani Akali Dal in August 1982?
options: A) A military alliance with Pakistan to establish an independent overseas cantonment
B) A nationwide strike by railway employees to demand nationalisation of private agriculture
C) An educational boycott demanding the closure of all universities in northern India
D) A mass political and civil disobedience agitation demanding the implementation of the Anandpur Sahib Resolution and greater provincial autonomy
questions.explanation: Launched in August 1982 under Sant Harchand Singh Longowal, the Dharam Yudh Morcha organized hundreds of thousands of Sikh volunteers courting arrest to press for the Anandpur Sahib demands.

questions.question: What was the political origin of the 'Plebiscite Front' formed in Jammu and Kashmir in 1955 under the patronship of Sheikh Abdullah?
options: A) It was launched by Mirza Afzal Beg following Sheikh Abdullah's arrest in 1953 to campaign for a popular plebiscite to determine Kashmir's future
B) It was created by the Maharaja Hari Singh to demand the return of the British monarchy to the valley
C) It was organized by the Communist Party of India to advocate the collectivization of apple orchards
D) It was a Hindu nationalist organization demanding the total abrogation of Article 370
questions.explanation: Founded in 1955 by Mirza Afzal Beg, the Plebiscite Front mobilized mass support demanding that a UN-supervised plebiscite be conducted in J&K, remaining active until the 1974 Indira-Sheikh Accord.

questions.question: What was the dramatic political impact of the 'Mandal vs Kamandir' politics that unfolded across northern India in the early 1990s?
options: A) It resulted in the complete merger of the Bharatiya Janata Party and the Janata Dal into a single party
B) It created a dual polarization: the mobilization of backward classes for social justice through reservation versus the consolidation of Hindu electoral identity around the Ram Janmabhoomi movement
C) It eliminated all caste identities from Indian electoral discourse in favor of class-based voting
D) It triggered the abolition of the multi-party democratic system in favor of indirect presidential rule
questions.explanation: 'Mandal' (OBC reservation politics) and 'Kamandir' (the Ram temple movement) reshaped Indian politics in the 1990s, defining the two competing axes of social justice and cultural nationalism.

questions.question: In the severe balance of payments crisis of May-July 1991, what extraordinary financial measure was the Chandra Shekhar government forced to take to avert sovereign default?
options: A) Selling the entire state-owned Indian Railways network to private foreign investors
B) Completely shutting down all domestic commercial banks for six months
C) Pledging 47 tonnes of gold reserves with the Bank of England and Bank of Japan to secure foreign exchange loans
D) Defaulting on all sovereign external debt obligations and leaving the IMF
questions.explanation: Facing foreign exchange reserves down to barely two weeks of imports, the Chandra Shekhar government physically airlifted gold to London and Tokyo to raise $405 million and prevent default.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: Why did Mikhail Gorbachev's dual reforms of Glasnost and Perestroika end up destroying the Soviet Union rather than reviving it?
options: A) They caused the Soviet armed forces to invade Western Europe and trigger a global thermonuclear war
B) They were immediately blocked by the United Nations Security Council under Chapter VII
C) They forced the Soviet Union to adopt the Chinese one-child demographic policy
D) They unleashed pent-up nationalist aspirations and public discontent while dismantling the coercive mechanisms of the Communist Party without creating an effective alternative system
questions.explanation: Glasnost exposed historical Soviet crimes and enabled suppressed nationalist passions in the republics to erupt openly, while Perestroika destroyed the planned distribution networks, accelerating systemic collapse.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: What was the primary achievement of the Single European Act (SEA) adopted by the European Community in 1986?
options: A) Establishing the legal framework and deadline (31 December 1992) for completing the European Single Market with free movement of goods, services, capital, and labor
B) Creating the unified nuclear arsenal of the European continent under French command
C) Abolishing all national flags and anthems across member nations in favor of the European anthem
D) Formally admitting all Eastern European nations into the Warsaw Pact
questions.explanation: The Single European Act (1986) dismantled thousands of remaining non-tariff barriers, laying the foundation for the four freedoms (free movement of goods, services, people, and capital) by 1992.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: What is the structural meaning of the 'Pillars of the European Union' established by the 1992 Maastricht Treaty?
options: A) The three geographical branches of European military commands stationed in Berlin, Paris, and Rome
B) The division of EU governance into three pillars: European Communities (supranational), Common Foreign and Security Policy (intergovernmental), and Justice and Home Affairs (intergovernmental)
C) The physical architectural marble columns supporting the European Court of Justice building in Luxembourg
D) The tripartite monetary alliance linking the US dollar, the British pound, and the Deutsche mark
questions.explanation: Maastricht created a three-pillar structure: Pillar 1 (EC treaties, single market), Pillar 2 (CFSP), and Pillar 3 (police and judicial cooperation in criminal matters).

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: What was the historical significance of the 'Six-Point Programme' declared by Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in 1966 for East Pakistan?
options: A) It demanded that Urdu be made the sole compulsory language in all Bengali schools
B) It proposed the immediate political merger of East Pakistan with the Indian state of West Bengal
C) It demanded radical regional autonomy for East Pakistan, including separate currencies, independent fiscal powers, and a regional militia, serving as the charter for Bangladesh's liberation
D) It called for the suspension of all trade between East Pakistan and Southeast Asia
questions.explanation: Sheikh Mujib's Six Points articulated East Pakistan's demand for full autonomy from West Pakistan's economic and military domination, becoming the rallying manifesto of the Awami League.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: How did the 26-year-long civil war between the Sri Lankan armed forces and the LTTE finally terminate in May 2009?
options: A) Through a negotiated peace treaty brokered by the UN Security Council creating an independent Tamil Eelam
B) Through the permanent annexation of the Jaffna peninsula by the Indian armed forces
C) Through a nationwide referendum in which Tamil citizens voted to abolish the LTTE
D) Through an all-out conventional military offensive by the Sri Lankan military that captured the LTTE's final stronghold and killed supreme commander Velupillai Prabhakaran
questions.explanation: The Sri Lankan military under President Mahinda Rajapaksa launched a massive offensive, crushing the LTTE militarily and killing Prabhakaran near Mullaitivu in May 2009.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: What is the specialized function of the World Bank's International Development Association (IDA), established in 1960?
options: A) Providing zero-to-low-interest concessional loans (known as 'credits') and grants to the world's poorest developing countries
B) Financing commercial space exploration satellites for OECD nations
C) Insuring private hedge funds against currency devaluations in emerging markets
D) Regulating international maritime tariffs for deep-sea container vessels
questions.explanation: Known as the World Bank's 'soft loan window', the IDA offers interest-free credits and grants with long repayment horizons to low-income countries to boost development.

questions.question: Which category of security concerns does 'global warming and climate change' fall under in contemporary international relations theory?
options: A) Traditional and Military Security
B) Non-traditional and Global Security
C) Unilateral Strategic Deterrence
D) Interstate Border Defense
questions.explanation: Climate change is a classic non-traditional and global security threat because its causes and impacts transcend sovereign borders and cannot be addressed through military weapons or national armies.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: What is the primary rationale behind designating the deep seabed and ocean floor beyond national territorial jurisdiction as the 'Common Heritage of Mankind'?
options: A) To prevent developing nations from ever sailing commercial merchant ships in the Pacific Ocean
B) To transfer the ownership of all marine fisheries exclusively to the UN Security Council
C) To ensure that mineral resources in international waters are exploited for the benefit of all humanity and not monopolized by technologically advanced states
D) To ban all submarine telecommunication internet cables between continents
questions.explanation: Coined in international maritime law and codified in the 1982 UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), the principle ensures that deep seabed minerals benefit all nations equitably.

questions.question: What is the primary contention of right-wing cultural critics against globalization in developing societies like India?
options: A) That globalization forces all developing countries to adopt orthodox Soviet-style communist state planning
B) That multinational companies prevent citizens from purchasing modern digital electronic goods
C) That international trade treaties mandate the complete closure of all local public schools
D) That Western consumerism, individualism, and pop culture erode traditional moral values, family structures, and indigenous cultural heritage
questions.explanation: Right-wing cultural critics worry that globalisation homogenizes culture into a Western consumerist mould (e.g., celebration of Valentine's Day, western dress), threatening indigenous cultural identities.

questions.question: The historic 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts passed in 1992 mandated which revolutionary democratic reform across Indian states?
options: A) Statutory constitutional recognition of rural Panchayati Raj institutions and urban Municipalities with mandatory 33% reservation for women
B) The abolition of state legislative assemblies in favor of direct central rule
C) The permanent reservation of 50% of parliamentary seats for regional party leaders
D) The replacement of the First-Past-The-Post electoral system with proportional representation
questions.explanation: The 73rd and 74th Amendments constitutionally recognized rural and urban local self-government, instituted mandatory regular five-year elections, and reserved one-third of all seats for women.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: What is the function of the 'Peacebuilding Commission' (PBC) created by the United Nations in 2005?
options: A) A military high command that conducts nuclear preemptive strikes against rogue states
B) An intergovernmental advisory body that supports peace efforts in conflict-affected countries and prevents nations from relapsing into war
C) An international court that prosecutes sovereign heads of state for monetary debt default
D) A secret intelligence agency that monitors international telecommunications networks
questions.explanation: Established by the 2005 World Summit, the UN Peacebuilding Commission assists countries emerging from violent conflict with reconstruction, institution-building, and sustainable recovery.

questions.question: Which of the following was the pivotal recommendation of the Gorwala Committee on Public Administration (1951) regarding the developmental planning machinery of independent India?
options: A) Recommending the complete replacement of all Indian civil servants with foreign corporate executives
B) Urging the abolition of the Indian Parliament in favor of an administrative council of governors
C) Warning against ministerial interference in public sector enterprises and emphasizing clean, merit-based administrative autonomy
D) Mandating that all district magistrates must be members of the ruling political party
questions.explanation: A.D. Gorwala's report on public administration in 1951 cautioned against political corruption and patronage in the newly expanding state sector, laying early guidelines for civil service ethics.

questions.question: What was the administrative role of the 'Emergency Administration' established in Jammu and Kashmir in October 1947 under Sheikh Abdullah?
options: A) Conducting a formal plebiscite under the supervision of the United Nations military observers
B) Formally annexing Gilgit and Baltistan to the Punjab provincial government
C) Organizing the mass eviction of all non-Kashmiri residents from the valley
D) Mobilizing popular civilian resistance against Pakistani tribal raiders while administering essential civil services following the Maharaja's flight to Jammu
questions.explanation: Maharaja Hari Singh appointed Sheikh Abdullah as Head of Emergency Administration on 30 October 1947; Abdullah organized the popular militia (National Conference Peace Brigade) to defend Srinagar.

questions.question: Which economist formulated the 'Wage-Goods Model' of development in 1956 as a direct alternative to the capital-goods Mahalanobis strategy of the Second Plan?
options: A) C.N. Vakil and P.R. Brahmananda
B) V.K.R.V. Rao and D.R. Gadgil
C) Amartya Sen and Jagdish Bhagwati
D) Kaushik Basu and Pranab Bardhan
questions.explanation: Economists C.N. Vakil and P.R. Brahmananda argued in 1956 that India should prioritize 'wage goods' (food, textiles, consumer necessities) to absorb surplus rural labor rather than heavy capital goods.

questions.question: What was the significance of the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty regarding the allocation of the six rivers of the Indus basin between India and Pakistan?
options: A) All six rivers were placed under joint military management with equal 50-50 volume sharing at all dams

B) India received exclusive rights to the three Eastern Rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej), while Pakistan received rights to the three Western Rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab), subject to specified Indian non-consumptive uses
C) Pakistan received exclusive sovereignty over all six rivers in exchange for monetary financial compensation to India
D) India retained all six rivers while granting Pakistan rights exclusively during monsoon flood months
questions.explanation: The treaty allocated the Eastern Rivers (Sutlej, Beas, Ravi) entirely to India and the Western Rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) to Pakistan, while allowing India limited run-of-the-river hydroelectric generation on western rivers.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: In which state did the defection of Rao Birender Singh from the Congress in 1967 lead to the formation of the first non-Congress coalition government under the Vishal Haryana Party?
options: A) Punjab
B) Uttar Pradesh
C) Haryana
D) Madhya Pradesh
questions.explanation: In 1967, Rao Birender Singh broke away from the Congress, formed the Vishal Haryana Party, and became Chief Minister leading the Samyukta Vidhayak Dal coalition in Haryana.

questions.question: Which significant statutory recommendation made by the Shah Commission of Inquiry (1978) led to constitutional safeguards against arbitrary emergency declarations?
options: A) Abolishing the post of Prime Minister during all periods of internal civil unrest
B) Mandating that the Chief Justice of India must countersign every presidential executive order
C) Prohibiting Parliament from ever amending Article 352 or Article 356 in the future
D) Requiring that the President can proclaim an emergency under Article 352 only after receiving a written decision of the Union Cabinet, not merely the Prime Minister's unilateral advice
questions.explanation: The Shah Commission exposed how the Emergency was imposed without Cabinet concurrence; this resulted in the 44th Amendment inserting the requirement of a written Cabinet decision.

questions.question: Under the 1985 Punjab Accord, why was the promised transfer of Chandigarh exclusively to Punjab on 26 January 1986 delayed and ultimately derailed?
options: A) Disputes arose over the simultaneous transfer of contiguous Hindi-speaking territories (Abohar and Fazilka) from Punjab to Haryana, as recommended by the Mathew Commission
B) The Supreme Court declared the Punjab Accord unconstitutional under Article 3
C) Chandigarh's municipal council voted unanimously to secede from the Indian Union
D) The armed forces occupied Chandigarh and declared permanent martial law in the city
questions.explanation: The Mathew Commission and subsequent Venkataramiah Commission failed to resolve the identification of contiguous Hindi-speaking villages in Punjab to be transferred to Haryana in exchange, stalling Chandigarh's transfer.

questions.question: In which landmark decision did the Supreme Court of India uphold the constitutional validity of the 27% OBC reservation while ruling that caste can be an acceptable indicator of social backwardness under Article 16(4)?
options: A) State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (1951)
B) Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992)
C) M.R. Balaji v. State of Mysore (1963)
D) T. Devadasan v. Union of India (1964)
questions.explanation: In Indra Sawhney, the 9-judge bench ruled that caste can be used to identify social backwardness provided economic criteria ('creamy layer') are applied to weed out affluent individuals.

questions.question: What was the legal rationale behind the Supreme Court's verdict in the Ayodhya title dispute (M. Siddiq v. Mahant Suresh Das) delivered in November 2019?
options: A) It ordered the disputed site to be declared a protected national archaeological park with no places of worship
B) It partitioned the land into three equal pieces among the Nirmohi Akhara, Ram Lalla, and Sunni Waqf Board
C) The Court used its extraordinary powers under Article 142 to grant the disputed site to a trust for a temple while awarding 5 acres of alternative land in Ayodhya to the Sunni Central Waqf Board
D) It directed the Central Government to hold a municipal referendum in the town of Ayodhya
questions.explanation: A unanimous 5-judge Constitution Bench held that the Hindu plaintiffs established possessory title over the inner courtyard, while invoking Article 142 to allot 5 acres of land to the Muslim parties.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: In December 1991, the leaders of eight additional Soviet republics met in which Central Asian capital to sign a protocol formally adhering to the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS)?
options: A) Tashkent, Uzbekistan
B) Ashgabat, Turkmenistan
C) Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan
D) Alma-Ata (Almaty), Kazakhstan
questions.explanation: On 21 December 1991, the Alma-Ata Protocol was signed by 11 of the 15 Soviet republics (excluding the Baltic states and Georgia), formalizing the demise of the USSR and expansion of the CIS.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: What is the specialized function of the 'Copenhagen Criteria' established by the European Council in 1993 for countries aspiring to join the European Union?
options: A) Setting strict prerequisites for accession: stable democratic institutions, rule of law, human rights, a functioning market economy, and capacity to adopt the acquis communautaire
B) Mandating that all candidate countries must maintain nuclear-powered aircraft carriers in the Baltic Sea
C) Requiring applicant nations to replace their national currencies with gold bullion within three months
D) Excluding any country whose population does not belong to the Scandinavian linguistic family
questions.explanation: The Copenhagen Criteria define whether an applicant country is eligible to join the EU, requiring democracy, rule of law, market economy, and adherence to EU obligations (acquis).

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: Which historic pact signed in 1996 resolved the long-standing dispute between India and Bangladesh over the sharing of the Ganga waters at Farakka Barrage?
options: A) Teesta Water Accord (signed by Rajiv Gandhi and H.M. Ershad)
B) Ganga Water Sharing Treaty (signed by H.D. Deve Gowda and Sheikh Hasina)
C) Brahmaputra Basin Protocol (signed by I.K. Gujral and Khaleda Zia)
D) Dhaka Border Demarcation Pact (signed by P.V. Narasimha Rao and Ziaur Rahman)
questions.explanation: On 12 December 1996, Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda and Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina signed the 30-year treaty for sharing Ganga waters at Farakka during the dry season.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: Under the UN Charter, what unique power does Article 99 confer upon the Secretary-General of the United Nations?
options: A) The power to unilaterally veto any resolution passed by the permanent five members of the Security Council
B) The power to dismiss the democratically elected head of government of any member state
C) The power to bring to the attention of the Security Council any matter which in his opinion may threaten the maintenance of international peace and security
D) The power to commandeer commercial merchant shipping during international maritime crises
questions.explanation: Article 99 is the Secretary-General's most significant political tool, empowering him to independently place grave threats to peace on the Security Council's agenda.

questions.question: Which international agreement signed in 1996 prohibits any nuclear weapon test explosion or any other nuclear explosion in any environment, but has failed to enter into force due to non-ratification by Annex 2 states?
options: A) Partial Test Ban Treaty (PTBT)
B) Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW)
C) Strategic Arms Limitation Treaty (SALT)
D) Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty (CTBT)
questions.explanation: The CTBT, adopted in 1996, bans all nuclear explosions; under Article XIV, it cannot enter into force until ratified by all 44 states listed in Annex 2 (including the US, China, India, Pakistan, and North Korea).

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: What is the core institutional mandate of the Global Environment Facility (GEF) established on the eve of the 1992 Rio Earth Summit?
options: A) Operating as a financial mechanism that provides grants and blended finance to developing countries for biodiversity, climate change, and international waters projects
B) Enforcing naval blockades against countries that fail to reduce greenhouse emissions
C) Managing the commercial privatization of world river basins and freshwater reservoirs
D) Levying mandatory carbon income taxes on citizens residing in developing countries
questions.explanation: The GEF serves as the financial mechanism for major multilateral environmental conventions (UNFCCC, CBD, UNCCD, Stockholm Convention), funding environmental projects in developing nations.

questions.question: In the critique of intellectual property rights under globalisation, what was the significance of the 2001 WTO Doha Declaration on TRIPS and Public Health?
options: A) It banned all developing nations from manufacturing generic pharmaceuticals for their domestic populations
B) It affirmed that the TRIPS agreement can and should be interpreted in a manner supportive of WTO members' right to protect public health and promote access to medicines (compulsory licensing)
C) It granted multinational pharmaceutical companies absolute immunity from local price controls in poor countries
D) It mandated that all patented medicines must be paid for in US gold reserves
questions.explanation: The Doha Declaration (2001) recognized the flexibility of TRIPS, affirming developing countries' sovereign right to issue compulsory licenses for manufacturing affordable generic medicines during public health crises.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the key provision of the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985, enacted to curb political defections in Parliament and State Assemblies?
options: A) Banning all non-Congress political parties from contesting general elections for 20 years
B) Mandating that any defecting legislator must be imprisoned for five years under preventive detention
C) Inserting the Tenth Schedule, which disqualifies an elected legislator who voluntarily gives up party membership or votes against party whip without prior permission
D) Transferring the power to conduct legislative elections to state governors
questions.explanation: The 52nd Amendment inserted the Tenth Schedule (Anti-Defection Law), disqualifying legislators who voluntarily resign from their party or defy party whips, with the Speaker/Chairman as the deciding authority.

questions.question: Which prominent Praja Socialist Party (PSP) leader authored the pioneering study 'Politics of Scarcity' and served as the Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission in the late 1960s?
options: A) Acharya Narendra Deva
B) N.G. Ranga
C) Minoo Masani
D) Asoka Mehta
questions.explanation: Asoka Mehta was a prominent socialist intellectual who joined the Planning Commission as Deputy Chairman in 1963 and later served as Minister for Planning and Petroleum in Indira Gandhi's cabinet.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: Which autonomous republic inside Georgia fought a secessionist war against Tbilisi in 1992-1993 with covert Russian military backing, resulting in ethnic cleansing of Georgian populations?
options: A) Abkhazia
B) Adjara
C) Gagauzia
D) Karakalpakstan
